## Task: TRD-001
TRD Reference: docs/TRD/TRD-2026-6a87c77f-frontmatter-yaml-escaping.md#trd-001
PRD Reference: docs/PRD/PRD-2026-6a87c77f-frontmatter-yaml-escaping.md#req-001

--- TRD Context ---
### 1.1 Chosen approach — Option A: `JSON.stringify` scalar helper at the existing emit seam

Keep the hand-built frontmatter lines in both transformers. Introduce one helper that folds a value
to a single line and quotes it via `JSON.stringify`, and route every emitted value through it.
Separately, add a parse check at `generateMarkdown()` — the single funnel every artifact already
passes through — and reuse that same check in `validate-all.js`.

```js
// scripts/lib/yaml-scalar.js
const foldScalar  = (v) => String(v).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const yamlScalar  = (v) => JSON.stringify(foldScalar(v));
```

**Why `JSON.stringify`:** a JSON string literal is a valid YAML 1.2 double-quoted scalar. The
escaping is therefore stdlib's, not ours — there is no hand-rolled quoting logic to get wrong, and
no "does this need quoting?" predicate. That predicate is precisely the defect in `packages/pi`
(PRD REQ-008).

**Verified** against eight adversarial inputs — mid-string `: `, bracket group with trailing
content, embedded newlines and blank lines, embedded double quotes and backslashes, a leading `*`
with `#`/`|`/`>`/`%`/`&`/`!` throughout, a bare `ensemble:feature`, leading/trailing whitespace,
and non-ASCII. All eight round-trip through `yaml.load` to the folded original exactly.

### 1.2 Alternatives considered

**Option B — serialize the frontmatter block with `js-yaml`'s `dump()`.**
Correct by construction with none of our own quoting logic, and measured to produce a *smaller*
diff than Option A (js-yaml quotes only when necessary, so previously-valid artifacts emit
byte-identically). Rejected on emitter-style coupling, measured empirically:

| Behaviour | `dump()` output | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-line description | emits a `\|` block scalar | valid YAML, but violates REQ-003's single-line requirement; needs pre-folding anyway |
| `tools: [Read, Write]` | restyled to a block sequence (`- Read`) | changes every agent artifact's shape |
| `last-updated: 2026-03-15` | newly quoted | js-yaml decides, we don't |

Each is individually tunable, but the result is our code negotiating with a general-purpose
emitter's heuristics for a seven-key flat map. Option A has no heuristics at all.

> **PRD correction:** PRD v1.0.1's non-goal states `yaml.dump()` would produce "a much noisier
> diff." That rationale is wrong — measurement shows the opposite. The conclusion (don't use it)
> still holds, on the emitter-coupling grounds above. PRD corrected to match in v1.0.2.

**Option C — inline the quoting separately in each transformer.** Rejected by PRD REQ-001: three
emitters already exist and `packages/pi`'s copy has already drifted into incorrectness. One helper,
one rule.

### 1.3 Two shapes that must not be conflated

The single highest-risk detail in this change. Two frontmatter keys look similar and are not:

| Key | Current emission | YAML type | Correct treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowed-tools` (command) | `allowed_tools.join(', ')` | **string** — `"Read, Write"` | `yamlScalar(joined)` — quote the whole joined string |
| `tools` (agent) | `[${tools.join(', ')}]` | **flow sequence** — `["Read","Write"]` | `[${tools.map(yamlScalar).join(', ')}]` — quote each element |

Quoting `tools` as a whole string would collapse a list into one string; bracketing `allowed-tools`
would promote a string into a list. Either silently changes tool permissions. Both are pinned by
dedicated ACs in TRD-002 and TRD-003.
Satisfies: REQ-001
PRD ACs: AC-001-1, AC-001-2

### 1.1 Chosen approach — Option A: `JSON.stringify` scalar helper at the existing emit seam

Keep the hand-built frontmatter lines in both transformers. Introduce one helper that folds a value
to a single line and quotes it via `JSON.stringify`, and route every emitted value through it.
Separately, add a parse check at `generateMarkdown()` — the single funnel every artifact already
passes through — and reuse that same check in `validate-all.js`.

```js
// scripts/lib/yaml-scalar.js
const foldScalar  = (v) => String(v).replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
const yamlScalar  = (v) => JSON.stringify(foldScalar(v));
```

**Why `JSON.stringify`:** a JSON string literal is a valid YAML 1.2 double-quoted scalar. The
escaping is therefore stdlib's, not ours — there is no hand-rolled quoting logic to get wrong, and
no "does this need quoting?" predicate. That predicate is precisely the defect in `packages/pi`
(PRD REQ-008).

**Verified** against eight adversarial inputs — mid-string `: `, bracket group with trailing
content, embedded newlines and blank lines, embedded double quotes and backslashes, a leading `*`
with `#`/`|`/`>`/`%`/`&`/`!` throughout, a bare `ensemble:feature`, leading/trailing whitespace,
and non-ASCII. All eight round-trip through `yaml.load` to the folded original exactly.

**Option B — serialize the frontmatter block with `js-yaml`'s `dump()`.**
Correct by construction with none of our own quoting logic, and measured to produce a *smaller*
diff than Option A (js-yaml quotes only when necessary, so previously-valid artifacts emit
byte-identically). Rejected on emitter-style coupling, measured empirically:

| Behaviour | `dump()` output | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-line description | emits a `\|` block scalar | valid YAML, but violates REQ-003's single-line requirement; needs pre-folding anyway |
| `tools: [Read, Write]` | restyled to a block sequence (`- Read`) | changes every agent artifact's shape |
| `last-updated: 2026-03-15` | newly quoted | js-yaml decides, we don't |

Each is individually tunable, but the result is our code negotiating with a general-purpose
emitter's heuristics for a seven-key flat map. Option A has no heuristics at all.

> diff." That rationale is wrong — measurement shows the opposite. The conclusion (don't use it)

emitters already exist and `packages/pi`'s copy has already drifted into incorrectness. One helper,
one rule.

|---|---|---|---|

title: Generated command frontmatter is unparseable YAML — 20 of 40 commands silently dropped at plugin load
description:
Found while dogfooding from C:\dev\CRIBs on 2026-08-07.

## Impact
Half the ensemble command surface never loads in ANY Claude Code session, in any repo, silently.
No warning is emitted. Because the .md files ARE present on disk, this looks exactly like a
failed/partial install — real time was repeatedly lost reinstalling plugins, which can never fix it.

Verified: predicted-loadable vs actually-loaded command counts match exactly for all 5 packages.
core 5/5 OK, e2e-testing 2/2 OK, development 8 of 18 load, product 5 of 13 load, git 0 of 2 load.
ensemble-git appearing to have NO commands at all is this bug.

## Root cause
The yaml->md generator emits unquoted YAML plain scalars for values that require quoting. Three
defect classes, one flaw:

1. argument-hint as a bracket group with trailing content (17 files)
     argument-hint: [prd-path] [--team] [--foundational]
   YAML parses [prd-path] as a flow sequence; trailing content after ] is a ParserError.
   A SINGLE bracket group ([trd-path-or-slug]) or a <angle> value parses fine — which is why
   the failures looked random.

2. description containing an unquoted ': ' (product/feature.md)
     description: Orchestrate the full idea-to-plan pipeline: create-prd, refine-prd, ...
   YAML reads it as a nested mapping. ScannerError.

3. description hard-wrapped onto a column-0 continuation line + a stray blank line before the
   next key (git/release.md, git/claude-changelog.md). YAML tries to parse the continuation as
   a new key. ScannerError.

A parse failure kills the ENTIRE frontmatter block, so the command is dropped wholesale.

## Affected
development (10): create-trd, create-trd-foreman, configure-team, implement-trd-beads,
analyze-requirements, validate-requirements, refine-beads, beads-build, beads-plan,
trd-dependency-graph
product (8): feature, reqnroll-tdd, generate-playwright-tests, generate-reqnroll-bindings,
generate-feature-tests, check-binding-drift, check-feature-drift, check-playwright-drift
git (2): release, claude-changelog

## Fix
Always emit description and argument-hint as QUOTED single-line scalars; never let the emitter
line-wrap them. Then add a build-step check that yaml-parses every generated .md frontmatter and
fails generation on error — that check alone would have caught all 20 at generation time.

## Branch note
Land this on a clean branch off main (NOT dev — dev is local dogfood aggregation and is never the
head of a PR) so it is PR-able upstream to Sunstone-Partners. This affects every ensemble user.

## Repro
Walk ~/.claude/plugins/cache/ensemble/**/commands/**/*.md, split on '---', yaml.safe_load the
frontmatter, print what raises. 20 of 40 raise.

## Note
The CRIBs machine's local plugin cache was hand-patched 2026-08-07 to unblock work (all 40 now
parse). That patch is disposable and any plugin reinstall wipes it. This bead is the real fix.
